Introduction

Technology is not useful just because it is new or popular.

A useful tool solves a real problem in a simple way.

It may save time, reduce stress, help you study, or support your work.

But every tool also has a cost: money, attention, learning time, privacy risk, or maintenance.

Choosing useful technology means looking at both the benefit and the trade-off.

What technology do you use every day?

Which tool or app saves you the most time?

Have you ever bought or downloaded something useful at first, but later stopped using it?

When do you think technology becomes a distraction instead of a help?

Practice

What is the first question you should ask before choosing technology?

The best first question is simple: what problem am I trying to solve?

Why is time saving not always a good reason to choose a tool?

Many people choose technology because it saves time.

What can make a helpful phone or app less useful?

Some technology helps people stay connected, but it can also steal attention.

What costs should people think about besides the first price?

When people compare technology, they often think only about the first price.

Why is privacy part of whether a tool is useful?

A technology can be very convenient and still be a bad choice if it creates privacy problems.

What does the phrase learning curve mean in this lesson?

Some technology looks useful but takes too long to learn.

Why can the same technology be useful for one person but not for another?

Useful technology is personal.

Summary

Choose one technology you use now, such as a phone feature, an app, or a work tool.

Give a clear judgment: is it useful for you or not?

Explain your reason using at least two points from the lesson, such as time saved, distraction, cost, privacy, learning curve, or maintenance.

Example of a real learner output:

This calendar app is useful for me because it helps me remember deadlines and appointments.

It is also simple to use, so I do not waste time learning it.

I would keep it because it solves a real problem in my daily life.
